notes: Expected parse of synthetic_google_patent.html; the step-5 parser must reproduce `document` exactly.

Metadata: doc_id from itemprop=publicationNumber; title from meta DC.title (whitespace-normalized); assignee from itemprop=assigneeOriginal; year from the meta DC.date WITHOUT scheme (publication date); language from the description lang attribute, lower-cased; url is whatever the caller passes (null here).

Text: whitespace (incl.  ) collapsed to single spaces and stripped; entities decoded; inline elements (sub, sup, b, i, figref, claim-ref, span) joined without spaces (M<sub>w</sub> -> Mw, cm<sup>2</sup> -> cm2); block elements (div, li, p, heading) separated by one space.
Paragraph IDs use the printed number in the `num` attribute (num=0041 -> p-0041, location [0041]), not the off-by-one `id` attribute. Unnumbered paragraphs get p-u001, p-u002... in document order.
A description-line whose num is 0000 and that wraps <tables> produces only table blocks, no paragraph block.

Tables: t-<n> from tables/@num (00001 -> t-1). All <table> pieces of one <tables> element are one table. A row with exactly one non-empty cell matching 'TABLE <n>' is the caption (t-<n>-cap). Rows whose cells are all empty are dropped. Remaining rows are numbered 1.. in order (t-1-r-1 ...). Cells are verbatim after whitespace normalization, empty cells kept as ''; text = ' | '.join(cells). Separate value rows whose label wraps ('Photoacid' / 'generator', both rows with their own values) are NOT merged.

Wrapped rows (rules in negative_lines.ingest.tables): a row continues the previous one if an upper cell is unfinished (unbalanced '(', trailing '-', '/', '=', ',' or a connective like 'by'/'parts') or if its label cell is empty and no column has complete values in both rows. Shorter rows are padded. Each group gets an extra table_row_merged block t-<n>-r-<a>-<b> placed after its physical rows (cells joined; no space after '/' or after '-' before lowercase), with source_rows; the physical rows get merged_into. render() shows the merged row instead of its physical rows. Table 3: rows 1-2 (header), 3-4 and 5-6 merge; row 7 (empty label, '—' vs '95') does not.
Claims: one block per top-level claim (num 00001 -> c-1, location 'Claim 1'), nested claim-text joined with spaces; claim-statement is dropped.
heading = text of the nearest preceding <heading> in the description (null for abstract, claims and heading blocks themselves). Table blocks inherit the heading before the table.

document.title: Negative-tone photosensitive resin composition and pattern forming method

blocks.text: A negative-tone photosensitive resin composition comprising a phenolic resin, a crosslinker and a photoacid generator gives high resolution at a low exposure dose.
This application claims priority to a synthetic application filed in 2024.
blocks.heading: TECHNICAL FIELD

blocks.text: The present invention relates to a negative-tone photosensitive resin composition for i-line lithography.
blocks.heading: TECHNICAL FIELD

blocks.text: The present invention is described in more detail by way of Examples. In the Examples, "parts" means parts by mass unless otherwise stated.
blocks.heading: EXAMPLES

blocks.text: Resin A: a copolymer of p-hydroxystyrene and styrene (molar ratio 80/20) having Mw of 8,000 and Mw/Mn of 1.6 was obtained.
blocks.heading: Synthesis Example 1

blocks.text: 100 parts of Resin A obtained in Synthesis Example 1, 10 parts of hexamethoxymethylmelamine (crosslinker C-1), 3.0 parts of PAG-1 and 0.3 parts of trioctylamine (Q-1) were dissolved in a mixed solvent of PGMEA/PGME (mass ratio 7/3) to a solids content of 30 wt%, and filtered through a 0.2 µm filter.
blocks.heading: Example 1

blocks.text: The composition was spin-coated on a silicon wafer treated with HMDS to a film thickness of 1.0 µm, pre-baked on a hot plate at 65° C. for 1 min and then at 95° C. for 3 min, exposed through a mask with an i-line (365 nm) contact aligner, post-exposure baked at 95° C. for 2 min, and developed by immersion in a 2.38 wt% TMAH aqueous solution at room temperature for 60 s.
blocks.heading: Example 1

blocks.text: A composition was prepared and evaluated in the same manner as in Example 1 except that PAG-2 described in paragraph [0042] was used instead of PAG-1, and the crosslinker was used in an amount of 15 parts.
blocks.heading: Example 2

blocks.text: A composition was prepared in the same manner as in Example 1 except that no crosslinker was used. The compositions are shown in Table 1.
blocks.heading: Comparative Example 1

blocks.text: Sensitivity (Eop) is the exposure dose (mJ/cm2) at which a 2 µm line-and-space pattern (1:1) is formed with the designed size. Resolution is the smallest line width resolved at Eop. The residue in unexposed areas was evaluated by SEM according to the following criteria.
blocks.heading: Evaluation

blocks.text: A: no residue in unexposed areas.
blocks.heading: Evaluation

blocks.heading: Evaluation

blocks.text: As shown in Table 2 and FIG. 3, the compositions of Examples 1 and 2 gave high sensitivity; the contrast curve of Example 1 in FIG. 3 shows the gel dose near the onset.
blocks.heading: Evaluation

blocks.text: 1. A negative-tone photosensitive resin composition comprising: (A) 100 parts by mass of a phenolic resin; (B) 1 to 20 parts by mass of a crosslinker; and (C) 0.5 to 10 parts by mass of a photoacid generator.
2. The composition according to claim 1, wherein the photoacid generator is a sulfonium salt.
